summary: This article explains what asteroids are, why most of them orbit in a belt between Mars and Jupiter, how they differ from icy comets, and how scientists track the ones that pass near Earth.
introduce: Draw two overlapping circles on the board and quickly compare two familiar things, such as a cat and a dog, with the class. Tell students that while reading “Asteroids: Rocky Leftovers of the Solar System” they will look for ways things are alike and different.

keyTerms.def: to travel around something in a curved path
a small piece broken off from something larger
the force that pulls objects toward each other

challengeTerms.def: to come together and combine into one larger mass or whole
relating to the sky or outer space
relating to the force that pulls objects toward each other

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that scientists should spend a lot of money tracking asteroids that pass near Earth? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Imagine you are an astronomer explaining asteroids to a younger student. Write a short explanation of three facts that show how asteroids are different from comets.
struggling: Pre-teach orbit, fragment, and gravity with pictures or gestures, then let weak readers fill in a T-chart of alike and different with sentence starters.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use coalesce, celestial, and gravitational in a short paragraph that compares two ideas from the article and explain which difference matters most.
